name: Doctoralia
tagline: A patient-facing directory of doctors and clinics with reviews and online appointment booking, plus paid profile and practice management tiers for practitioners.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Doctoralia (Docplanner group) sells practitioner subscriptions that vary heavily by country and clinic size, and the figures are not published cleanly.

verdictSummary: The booking widget is the easy part: a calendar, slot rules, a confirmation email, done in an afternoon. What a doctor actually buys is patients who were already searching Doctoralia for a dermatologist in their city, plus the review history attached to their name. You cannot one-shot demand. Add health data handling, local medical advertising rules, and SMS reminder deliverability, and the consolation build is a clinic booking page, not a replacement. Fine if you already have the patients and just want to stop doing phone scheduling.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted booking page for one practice: define services and working hours, let patients pick a free slot, store the appointment, and email both sides a confirmation.
requirements: A domain and somewhere to host it
An SMTP provider for confirmation emails (and an SMS provider if you want reminders)
Your own patient flow: people must already know your practice exists
A real look at local rules before you store anything clinical
whatYouLose: Patient discovery: the search traffic that makes the listing worth paying for
Accumulated public reviews and the ranking they feed
Insurance, specialty and location filters that patients actually browse by
SMS reminder infrastructure with decent delivery rates and no-show reduction data
Practice management extras: multi-practitioner calendars, patient records, payments, support in your language
moatNotes: Two sided and geographically fragmented: being big in Poland, Spain, Italy or Brazil is the product, and a local clone starts with zero patients on day one.
whyPeopleStillPay: Doctors do not pay for a calendar, they pay to be found. A clinic that drops the subscription keeps its appointment slots and loses the stream of strangers who typed a specialty and a city into Google and landed on a Doctoralia profile with 200 reviews. The reviews are the other half: they are hosted there, they do not come with you, and starting a fresh review history at zero is a worse marketing problem than the subscription cost. For an established practice with a full book and word of mouth, cancelling makes sense and a self-hosted booking page covers the rest. For anyone growing, the fee is a customer acquisition line item.
notes: The booking form is a weekend; the patients are not. The moat is marketplace liquidity in specific countries plus the review history that stays behind when you leave.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted appointment booking page for a single medical practice. This is a scheduling tool, not a directory: no patient-facing search across practitioners, no reviews, no marketplace.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/app.db, schema created on first run
- Nodemailer for email, SMTP credentials from .env
- Deployed as a single long-running Node process, no serverless assumptions

Data model:
- practitioners: id, name, title, bio
- services: id, practitioner_id, name, duration_minutes, price, buffer_minutes
- availability_rules: practitioner_id, weekday, start_time, end_time
- blackouts: practitioner_id, starts_at, ends_at, reason
- appointments: id, service_id, practitioner_id, starts_at, ends_at, patient_name, patient_email, patient_phone, reason_note, status (booked | cancelled | completed), cancel_token

Public flow at /book:
1. Pick a service, 2. pick a practitioner, 3. see a two-week grid of free slots, 4. enter name, email, phone and a short reason, 5. confirm.
Slot generation runs server side from availability_rules minus blackouts minus existing appointments including buffers. Never trust slots sent by the client: re-check on submit inside a transaction and return a clear conflict error.

Emails: confirmation to patient with an .ics attachment and a cancel link using cancel_token, plus a notification to the practice inbox. Add a /api/cron/reminders route protected by a shared secret that emails anyone with an appointment in the next 24 hours.

Admin at /admin behind a single password from .env (HTTP-only session cookie, no user accounts): day and week calendar, manual booking, cancel, blackout editor, service and availability editor.

Keep clinical data out. The reason_note is one short free-text line, label it clearly as non-confidential, and do not add file uploads, diagnoses or records. No analytics, no telemetry, no third-party scripts.

Ship with a seed script creating one practitioner, three services and Mon-Fri hours, a README covering .env vars and SQLite backup, and a note in the README that storing patient data may trigger local health privacy rules.
